subject: Pediatrics
title: Neonatal Resuscitation: Ventilation Comes First
preview: At birth, evaluate breathing and heart rate while preventing heat loss; effective ventilation is central when resuscitation is needed.

sections.title: Prepare and assess
points: Anticipate risk, assemble the team and equipment, support thermoregulation and use appropriate cord management.
Use pulse oximetry to guide oxygen titration when needed.

sections.title: Correct ventilation first
points: Mask seal, airway positioning and effective lung inflation are prerequisites to judging the response.
If bradycardia persists despite optimized ventilation, escalate via the current neonatal life-support algorithm.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Ineffective ventilation is a common correctable cause of persistent neonatal bradycardia.
Chest compressions are not the first response for every noncrying newborn.

quickRevision: Most newborns transition without resuscitation; assess breathing, tone and heart rate in an appropriate neonatal setting.
When assisted ventilation is needed, effectiveness is indicated by a rising heart rate.
If the heart rate fails to improve, reassess the airway and ventilation before escalating to compressions and other measures.

quiz.question: What is central to effective initial neonatal resuscitation?
options: Immediate chest compressions for all babies
Routine high-dose glucose for every newborn
quiz.explanation: Establishing effective ventilation. If bradycardia persists despite optimized ventilation, escalate via the current neonatal life-support algorithm.
